records.title: The New York Post endorses President Donald J. Trump for re ...
records.retrieval_query: Did the New York Post publish an editorial or endorsement of Donald Trump's re-election bid, and on what date?

passages.P1: We can return to the explosive job creation, rising wages and general prosperity we had before the pandemic. We can have economic freedom and opportunity, and resist cancel culture and censorship. We can put annus horribilis, 2020, behind us and make America great again, again. We can do all this — if we make the right choice on Nov. 3.
passages.P2: The New York Post endorses President Donald J. Trump for re-election.
passages.P4: Elections are always about the economy, but never more so than this year.
passages.P5: So a reminder: Until the necessary shutdown to fight the coronavirus, the unemployment rate stood at 3.5 percent, the lowest in a half-century. African American unemployment was 6.8 percent, the lowest figure since 1972.
passages.P6: Adults out of the workforce for years found new prospects; for 17 months of Trump’s term, there were 1 million more job openings than people unemployed.
passages.P7: That drove up salaries. For the first time in a decade, wage growth exceeded 3 percent year-over-year. It also narrowed the wealth gap. Between 2016 and 2019, real median incomes rose the most, 9 percent, for those without a high school diploma. Real median incomes declined 2.3 percent for those with a college degree, mostly because older workers retired, according to the Federal Reserve’s Survey of Consumer Finances.
passages.P8: How did President Trump do it? First, by trusting the free market. He championed lowering the corporate tax rate to a figure more in line with the rest of the industrialized world. He cut cumbersome regulations, particularly ones rammed through as President Barack Obama was headed out the door. He streamlined the permitting process that would delay infrastructure projects by years, sometimes decades.
passages.P9: A Joe Biden administration would be beholden to a socialist left that sees an opportunity to remake the nation in its vision, one more dependent on government debt. Consider Biden’s dance on fracking — against it for his party, in favor of it in general because he knows what a positive force it’s been for Pennsylvania. Which position would he have in office?
passages.P10: Trump also rejected the globalist axiom that trade deals and unfettered immigration were better for Americans. The US has lost 3.7 million jobs to China since 2001, according to the Economic Policy Institute. And this undermining of our workers with cheap foreign labor did nothing to encourage openness and democracy in Beijing. China’s authoritarianism has only grown worse with concentration camps for Uighurs, crackdowns in Hong Kong and the shuttering of independent churches. The nation remains a manipulative planned economy that devalues its currency and exploits its trade deficit.
passages.P11: Further, the president recognized that unfettered illegal immigration was unfair to American workers, a common-sense belief held by such right-wingers as Bernie Sanders.
passages.P12: Biden would open the border floodgates again, and by all appearances would go back to “normalization” with China — a byword for them eating our lunch.
passages.P14: Domestically, President Trump has rolled back the excesses of previous administrations.

records.title: Fact check: NY Post encourages Trump to accept Biden's victory
records.retrieval_query: Did the New York Post publish an editorial or endorsement of Donald Trump's re-election bid, and on what date?

passages.P3: # Fact check: After endorsing him, New York Post now pushes Trump to accept Biden's victory
passages.P7: ## The claim: New York Post published a cover and staff editorial urging President Donald Trump to accept defeat
passages.P8: On Oct. 26, the New York Post endorsed President Donald Trump's bid for reelection.
passages.P9: The cover of the tabloid that announced the choice was emblazoned with a photo of Trump and the words, "Make America great again, again."
passages.P10: On Dec. 28, another cover of the New York Post dedicated to Trump appeared online, posted to Instagram by accounts like PoliAlert and Breaking 911. This cover, though, had a very different message: "Mr. President... STOP THE INSANITY. You have lost the election — here's how to save your legacy."
passages.P11: PoliAlert and Breaking 911 have not responded to requests from USA TODAY for comment.
passages.P12: ## Both the cover and editorial are real
passages.P13: Both the cover and staff editorial that are critical of Trump are real, published by the New York Post on Dec. 27.
passages.P14: The tabloid, owned by Rupert Murdoch, published the front page online along with a copy of the editorial, which ran under the headline, "The Post says: Give it up, Mr. President — for your sake and the nation’s."
passages.P15: The scathing editorial instructed Trump to "end this dark charade" and accused him of "cheering for an undemocratic coup" by encouraging Republicans to reject the results of the presidential contest.
passages.P16: "You had every right to investigate the election. But let’s be clear: Those efforts have found nothing," the editorial read.
passages.P17: It also took aim at his allies, including lawyer Sidney Powell, whom it called "a crazy person," and Michael Flynn, a retired lieutenant general – who it said committed acts "tantamount to treason" by suggesting Trump should institute martial law rather than accept the electoral results and leave office peacefully.
passages.P18: Instead of disputing his loss, the editorial encouraged Trump to focus on the upcoming runoff elections in Georgia on Jan. 5 that will decide control of the Senate.
passages.P19: "Securing the Senate means securing your legacy. You should use your considerable charm and influence to support the Georgia candidates, mobilizing your voters for them," the editorial read. "Focus on their success, not your own grievances, as we head into the final week."
passages.P20: The editorial concluded with the following warning for Trump, a quote that PoliAlert also included in its post on Instagram:
passages.P21: "If you insist on spending your final days in office threatening to burn it all down, that will be how you are remembered. Not as a revolutionary, but as the anarchist holding the match."
passages.P22: The New York Post has long bolstered Trump — both while he became a celebrity in New York City and early in the primaries in 2016, per the New York Times.
passages.P23: Still, its tone has shifted since it became clear that President-elect Joe Biden had clinched a victory. For example, on Nov. 7, the New York Post issued a staff editorial that instructed Trump to "stop the ‘stolen election’ rhetoric."

records.title: NY Post endorses Trump after previous criticisms
records.retrieval_query: What exact wording did any New York Post endorsement use regarding Donald Trump's re-election, and was it an official editorial board endorsement?

passages.P2: # NY Post endorses Trump after previous criticisms
passages.P6: Republican presidential nominee former President Trump dances at a campaign rally at Greensboro Coliseum, Oct. 22, 2024, in Greensboro, N.C.
passages.P7: The New York Post is endorsing former President Trump for president, arguing his record in the White House matters more than his tendency to be “ridiculously hyperbolic.”
passages.P8: Writing that Trump “exhibits the same strength and vigor as he did in 2016,” the Post’s editorial board said Trump and Harris “want to take us down very different roads — making the choice stark and simple, but vital.”
passages.P9: “Donald Trump is the right choice,” the Rupert Murdoch-owned newspaper wrote.
passages.P10: The Post’s endorsement comes after previous criticisms the outlet’s editorial board has hurled at Trump over his managing of the COVID-19 pandemic and actions in the lead-up to the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol by his supporters.
passages.P11: CNN media critic Brian Stelter noted Friday that in in 2022, the Post said Trump had “proven himself unworthy to be this country’s chief executive again.”
passages.P12: The newspaper has changed its tune less than two weeks out from election day.
passages.P13: “His opponents focus on how Trump’s administration was marked by a relentless soap opera of high drama and chaos — much of which they fueled. And yes, many find him offensive — and we say fair enough: He can be ridiculously hyperbolic,” the Post wrote in its endorsement.
passages.P14: “But before COVID wreaked havoc across the globe, Trump’s first-term results were paychecks that grew markedly faster than inflation, the lowest unemployment in 50 years, a secure border and peace overseas.”
passages.P15: Trump has feuded with Murdoch and a number of the conservative media outlets he owns for months, most notably attacking the Post over its glowing coverage of Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) during the GOP presidential primary.
passages.P16: But Friday morning, Trump shared the newspaper’s cover story on his Truth Social website, showing a photo of him raising his fist for a crowd in Pennsylvania after being shot in an assassination attempt earlier this year.
passages.P17: “I LOVE THE NEW YORK POST,” he wrote.

records.title: Donald Trump Gets Good News From Home State Newspaper
records.retrieval_query: What exact wording did any New York Post endorsement use regarding Donald Trump's re-election, and was it an official editorial board endorsement?

passages.P4: Newsweek is a Trust Project member
passages.P5: See more of our trusted coverage when you search.to see more of our trusted coverage when you search.
passages.P6: Donald Trump has been endorsed in the 2024 election by the *New York Post*, a conservative tabloid based in the former president's home state.
passages.P7: *The Post*'s front page on Friday featured the headline "Back to the Future" alongside a photo of Trump. In an article explaining their endorsement, *The Post*'s editorial board said the former president is the "clear choice for a better future."
passages.P8: Trump has cited *The Post* as his "favorite" newspaper, although the Rupert Murdoch-owned publication has been critical of the Republican in recent years. In December 2020, the paper ran a front page urging Trump to "stop the insanity" and accept that he lost the previous month's election to Joe Biden.
passages.P10: The publication also blamed Trump for the Republican Party's underwhelming 2022 midterm performance. The GOP failed to win control of the Senate and only managed a narrow majority in the House after Trump's MAGA and election-denying candidates lost their races across the country.
passages.P12: *The Post's* editorial board is now backing Trump over Democratic nominee Kamala Harris in the 2024 election while saying the former president could repeat the success of his first term in office on issues such as the economy and immigration.
passages.P13: *Newsweek* has contacted Trump's and Harris' offices via email for comment.
passages.P14: "To borrow from Ronald Reagan's famous 'Are you better off now than you were four years ago?': Voters should ask themselves if they were better off under Trump or Joe Biden and Kamala Harris," the editorial board wrote.
passages.P15: "His opponents focus on how Trump's administration was marked by a relentless soap opera of high drama and chaos—much of which they fueled.
passages.P16: "And yes, many find him offensive—and we say fair enough: He can be ridiculously hyperbolic.
passages.P17: "But before COVID wreaked havoc across the globe, Trump's first-term results were paychecks that grew markedly faster than inflation, the lowest unemployment in 50 years, a secure border and peace overseas."
passages.P18: The board also dismissed concerns about Trump's age and cognitive ability hindering his ability to run for a second term. They said the former president "exhibits the same strength and vigor as he did in 2016, despite the unprecedented and disgraceful weaponization of the justice system against him, two assassination attempts and the all-too-familiar constant barrage of hysterical media attacks on him."
passages.P19: Trump, 78, is the oldest presidential nominee in U.S. history. If the Republican wins November's election, he could overtake Biden as the oldest-ever sitting U.S. president during his second term.
passages.P20: "The burden is heavy on our shoulders this November," *The Post*'s editorial board added. "But Trump and Harris want to take us down very different roads—making the choice stark and simple, but vital. Donald Trump is the right choice."
passages.P21: *The Post* was previously warming more to Trump's rival, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, who challenged the former president in the 2024 GOP primary.
passages.P22: The day after the 2022 midterm elections, *The Post* featured DeSantis on its front page following his resounding reelection victory with the headline "DeFUTURE."
